proposed_widenings.name: activated_magic_item_ongoing_aura
proposed_widenings.justification: The item combines existing passive held mechanics with an activated, time-bounded, location-anchored aura that continuously grants benefits to creatures in an illuminated area. Magic items currently admit only passive, activation, or composite(passive|activation), and activation phases are one-shot rather than persistent ongoing area states.
proposed_widenings.evidence: As a Magic action, you can plant the haft end of the rod in the ground ... While in that Bright Light, you and your allies gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class and saving throws ... The rod's head stops glowing and the effect ends after 10 minutes or when a creature takes a Magic action to pull the rod from the ground.

proposed_widenings.name: non_spell_location_anchor_for_activated_effects
proposed_widenings.justification: The aura is centered on the planted rod, not on the wielder, and ends when the rod is pulled from the ground. Existing activated abilities do not have a non-spell location/object anchor or an early-end trigger for removing that anchor.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you can plant the haft end of the rod in the ground ... when a creature takes a Magic action to pull the rod from the ground

proposed_widenings.name: visibility_limited_invisible_sense
proposed_widenings.justification: Existing senses can model seeing invisible creatures broadly, but this rider is narrower: creatures in the aura can sense the location of invisible creatures only while both are in the bright-light area. That conditional area-scoped detection is not an existing authored shape.
proposed_widenings.evidence: While in that Bright Light, you and your allies ... can sense the location of any Invisible creature that is also in the Bright Light.

notes: The held Alertness bonus and held spell list both fit existing surface pieces (`holding_item`, `modify_roll_advantage`, `grant_spell_access`). The blocker is the planted Protective Aura, which would require a persistent non-spell aura family rather than a one-shot activation placeholder.
